strategies.rule: With >= 3 days to close and the YES ask or bid at or below 0.45, compare price with a reference probability that rises linearly to 0.5 as close time approaches. Buy YES if reference - price >= 0.06; buy NO if price - reference >= 0.06.

Look at the last 6 snapshots. If YES mid rose by >= 0.03 and the last three snapshots are not lower, buy YES at the ask while it is below 0.9. Symmetric for NO on a fall. Exit is handled by the portfolio's take-profit.

Needs >= 10 snapshots and >= 50 contracts resting on each side. If YES mid is at least 0.05 above its window mean, buy NO; if it is at least 0.05 below, buy YES. Intended as a resting-order (maker) style entry.

When the |change| in YES mid between consecutive snapshots is >= 0.1, buy in the direction of the jump at the touch, provided the price has not already retraced more than 0.05 from the post-jump level.

Within a topic, buy YES at the ask on markets with >= 25 contracts resting per side whose YES price is at or below 0.4: positive-expectation longshots the market still prices as live rather than dead.

Buying YES and NO together costs (1 - NO bid) + (1 - YES bid) = 2 - (YES bid + NO bid) and pays exactly $1 at settlement, so a locked edge exists only when YES bid + NO bid exceeds 1 by at least 0.03. Enter when both sides rest >= 25 contracts.

disclaimer: Simulated fills on observed quotes. Not exchange trades, no Kalshi account involved, and no slippage beyond the quoted touch is modelled.
